subject: PrivDeploy payment phasing, platform fee annualization & SLA credit outline
messages:

Cc: procurement@stratahealth.com
Date: 2027-06-30T14:02:00Z
Subject: PrivDeploy commercial clarifications - StrataHealth

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about the Private/VPC option. Procurement has a short list of commercial questions that will determine whether we go annual-committed or start with a hybrid pilot. Attached is our procurement questionnaire and a draft SOW to speed review. Key items we need clarified:

- Platform fee: can this be annualized and amortized over the term, or do you require the full platform fee upfront? If amortizable, what accounting/contract language do you propose?
- Licensing: operator/site licenses — can we convert between them mid-term and what credits apply?
- Support tiers & SLA credits: what are the response tiers for on-call vs standard support and how are service credits calculated?
- Escrow: for air-gapped/on-prem builds, do you offer any code or build escrow?

We'd like a short written reply that lays out 2–3 packaging options and one recommended path for our CFO. Also happy to jump on a 30–45 minute sync.

Attached: Strata_Procurement_Questionnaire.pdf; draft_SOW_Strata-Redwood_v0.9.docx

Best,
Laura Jenkins
Sr. Procurement Manager | StrataHealth
laura.jenkins@stratahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy commercial clarifications - StrataHealth

Laura — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Quick summary of how we normally structure these and three packaging paths for your finance team to consider:

Option A — Annual committed model (recommended for unit-cost predictability)
- One platform fee billed annually, with an in-contract amortization schedule we can add (accounting-friendly language).
- Operator licenses purchased up front; conversion to site license allowed at 75% credit of remaining license value.
- Support Tier 2 included; Tier 3 (SRE) add-on. SLA credits: sliding scale with 10% monthly cap.

Option B — Hybrid pilot -> commit
- Small pilot platform fee (pro-rated) for first 3 months + monthly metered usage. If you convert to annual within 90 days we apply pilot fees as a credit toward the annual platform fee.
- Operator licenses can be temporarily provided as trial operators; conversion credits at a fixed schedule.

Option C — Consumption-first with rollover credits
- No large upfront platform fee; monthly usage floor + small monthly platform base. Yearly true-up with credits applied against overage.

Next steps I propose: I will run a quick commercial examples spreadsheet that models amortization and credit math for the three options and Naomi will sketch the SLA credit matrix. Can you confirm whether Strata prefers operator-license economics (per engineer/operator) or site-license economics (per site/GPU pool)? Once we have that, we'll produce a redlineable SOW and a suggested term sheet.

Attaching a short table of examples. Happy to take a call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwoodinference.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-07-01T10:01:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy commercial clarifications - SLA and support detail

Adding support/SLA detail and a couple of guardrails from finance/ops:

- Support tiers:
  - Standard (business hours) — 8x5 email + 4hr response for Sev 1
  - Premium (24x7 SRE add-on) — 1hr response Sev 1, 4hr Sev 2
  - Escalation paths and on-call rotation described in SOW appendix B.
- SLA credits: credits are calculated as a % of the monthly platform fee only (not usage). We typically cap credits at 30% of the monthly platform fee and a maximum single-event credit of 15%. For multi-day outages we apply per-day buckets.
- Operator <-> Site license conversion: finance requires a conversion schedule (e.g., 75% credit on remaining term for operator->site, 50% for site->operator). We can make an exception for pilot conversions if you commit to >12-month term.
- Escrow: we can support code/build escrow for on-prem major release artifacts via third-party escrow. We will provide standard escrow terms and can add a carve-out for security-sensitive builds.

I'm attaching our SLA_credit_matrix.pdf (simple examples). We'll include explicit amortization language in the SOW so your accounting team can model it.

Naomi Feldman
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-07-01T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy commercial clarifications - concession idea

Laura — a quick add from the commercial team:

If Strata is willing to commit to a 12-month minimum capacity (we can define the GPU/node floor), we are prepared to offer a 25% pilot discount (first 90 days) and treat the pilot fees as a credit toward the annual platform fee. That concession unlocks tighter unit pricing and accelerates support SLAs to the Premium tier for the pilot period.

On escrow: for air-gapped installs we typically suggest third-party escrow (IronClad Escrow or equivalent) and include a limited extraction procedure in the SOW. We do not put nightly builds in escrow, only major release binaries and build instructions. We can provide sample escrow language for legal.

If you have any non-negotiables from procurement/legal, flag them and we'll fold them into the redline. Otherwise we'll generate the draft redline SOW and the amortization examples Naomi mentioned.

—David
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
